title: API pocket runbook: timeouts, 429s, streaming degradations
content:
Purpose:
Quick, chewable runbook for on-call SREs to triage the four most common API failure modes we see: request timeouts, 429 (rate-limit/quota) spikes, degraded streaming (chunk delays / partial responses), and elevated error rates (5xx/4xx surges). This is intentionally concise — use the full playbooks for deep follow-ups.

Scope / when to use: 
- Pager firing for api-availability, api-5xx-rate, api-streaming-latency, or sustained 429 alert.
- Customer reports of partial responses or long tail latencies.
- Not for planned maintenance or known deploys (check deploy calendar first).

Quick mindset: measure -> isolate -> mitigate -> restore -> communicate. If uncertain, escalate early.

Immediate triage checklist (first 5–10 minutes):
- Check primary dashboards: API ingress QPS, 50/95/99 latency, 5xx/4xx rates, streaming chunk latency (ms), active connections.
- Confirm scope: global vs single region vs single route. Use the route filter.
- Identify recent deploys: last 30m. Query deploy service: git commit, CI status.
- Look at capacity/queue/backpressure: GPU pool utilization, request queue length, sustained CPU at >80%.
- Note customers impacted (SLA tiers). Tag incident as P0/P1.

Useful dashboards / queries (one-liners to paste):
- Time-series: api.requests.count{route:*} by route, region, model_variant, status_code
- Latency: p99(api.request.duration) by route and model_variant over 30m
- Streaming: histogram(stream.chunk.latency_ms) last 15m, count of connection resets
- Quota: rate_limit.rejections{client_id} top 20 in last 10m
- Backpressure: serving.request_queue_length, serving.pool_utilization{pool} over 10m

CLI / debug commands (service names are examples):
- kubectl -n inference logs deploy/api-gateway -c proxy --since=10m | tail -200
- kubectl -n inference exec -it deploy/edge-proxy -- /bin/sh -c 'ss -tnp | grep 443'
- ./infra/observe/query_metrics --metric api.requests.count --filter 'route=chat' --range 15m
- curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY' "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health"

Failure-mode specific guidance:
1) Timeouts (inbound requests timing out or p99 latency ballooning)
   Evidence: p95/99 latency spikes, request_queue_length increasing, downstream model calls blocking, client-side timeouts.
   Likely causes: model serving saturation, blocking sync work (disk/DB), slow network to model host, bad batching configuration.
   Fast mitigations:
     - Shift traffic to lower-latency model variant or region via routing control (route->fallback model in runtime).
     - Reduce request batch sizes / disable large-batch policy for the affected route (temporary config flip).
     - Increase replica count / scale up dedicated pool if autoscaler is lagging (follow autoscale runbook).
     - Enable prefix/KV cache for very hot prompts to short-circuit work.
   Longer follow-up: analyze model-level kernel metrics, look at mem/GPU stalls, inspect recent quantization changes.

2) 429 spikes (rate limit or quota rejections)
   Evidence: sudden rise in 429 status codes; tops of queue for specific client_id; per-key throttling logs.
   Likely causes: bursty client traffic, regression in token accounting, misconfigured rate limit policy, downstream capacity causing upstream throttle.
   Fast mitigations:
     - Identify top offender client_ids via rate_limit.rejections metric. POST to SRE slack #sre-incidents with client id(s) and TTL for temporary overrides.
     - Apply short-lived quota bump or whitelist for affected enterprise customers (use internal admin portal).
     - If broad, enable soft-degradation: reduce max_tokens limit globally or apply global per-request size cap.
     - If rate-limiter misbehavior suspected, flip to permissive mode (controlled) and monitor.
   Notes: make overrides timeboxed and recorded in incident notes. Follow up with product/CS for true root cause.

3) Degraded streaming (long gaps between chunks, partial responses, connection resets)
   Evidence: stream.chunk.latency_ms histogram shifted right, connection reset counts, client errors about truncated streams.
   Likely causes: long-tail token generation stall in runtime, KV cache miss penalties, network flaps, aggressive proxy timeouts.
   Fast mitigations:
     - Force-fallback to non-streaming response for high-risk routes (return full response via sync path) to restore user experience.
     - Toggle keepalive timeout between proxy and runtime (increase briefly).
     - Check proxies/load balancer health; restart suspect proxies in a staggered manner.
     - If GC/pause suspected on runtime host, cordon node and shift traffic.
   Example quick check: review tracer spans for stream-send times; search for 'token_generation_delay' tags.

4) Elevated error rates (5xx surge, unexpected 4xx)
   Evidence: traffic-level 5xx spike; auth-related 4xx may point to upstream auth service.
   Likely causes: bad deploy, config flag bug, dependency outage (auth, billing, feature store), model OOMs.
   Fast mitigations:
     - Rollback recent deploys for the implicated route (use canary history).
     - Toggle fail-open vs fail-closed for optional features (safety filters, rerankers) to isolate.
     - If OOMs or model crashes: drain and restart pool nodes one at a time; enable a smaller model variant.
     - If dependency is failing, enable degraded mode that returns cached or best-effort responses with a clear response metadata flag.

Communications checklist (first 15–30m):
- Post to #sre-incidents with short summary (impact, scope, mitigation in progress, ETA for next update).
- If customer-impacting and enterprise tier involved, notify CSM and Sales with customer list and suggested mitigations.
- Record all temporary config flips and overrides in the incident notes with TTL.

Escalation matrix:
- On-call SRE -> SRE lead (if >15m unresolved and customer-impacting) -> Eng on-call for serving/runtime -> Product owner for routing decisions -> Exec if >1h with >10% error rate or >SLA breach.

Postmortem tags / required follow-ups (when resolving):
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence.
- Timeline with deploys, config flips, mitigation steps.
- Customer impact list and minutes of outage.
- Action items: test coverage gaps, alert tuning changes, runtime metrics to add, playbook updates.

Runbook TODOs / open questions (notes to self):
- Add a short canned script to automatically list top 10 client_ids by 429 in last 5m.
- Improve streaming tracer tags for 'awaiting_next_token' to differentiate model vs network stalls.
- Revisit global defaults for streaming keepalives across cloud regions.
- Define safe memory pressure thresholds per model variant (we keep hitting OOMs without clear signals).

Example mini incident snippet (for quick copy):
- 09:03: pager api-p99-latency fired for prod-us-west-2 (p99 6.2s). Root cause: large batch policy misapplied to chat-route after recent rollout. Mitigation: disabled large-batch for chat-route at 09:09 (latency back to 0.9s p99 by 09:15). Next: add pre-deploy check for batch policy changes.

Final note: this is a pocket guide — we should keep it short on the page (oncall-friendly). For any action that mutates infra (scaling, whitelist, permissive-rate-limiter), ALWAYS pair with a rollback step and clock TTL into incident notes.

Unresolved / WIP: can we automate a safe 'slow-mode' that both reduces global token limit and routes heavy clients to best-effort fallback model automatically? Filed SRE-3421 to prototype.

References & links: full playbooks, metrics dashboards, and SLO definitions are in the linked artifacts above.

----
Notes to self (scratch):
- shorthand: p99=99thpct, qps=queries/sec, kv=prefix cache, rt=runtime, gpupool=dedicated-pool-A
- keep short examples and commands so oncall can copy/paste.
